task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-06-16, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
Adhering to a suppression-conditional recommended mix predicts winning.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 54 series

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: Does adherence to a recommended play-type mix predict game or series wins out of sample?
Is the recommended mix derived from point outcomes, creating circularity with winning?
Are suppression estimates reliable given limited per-opponent possessions?
Is 54 series adequately powered, and how is team-quality confounding handled?
Is any result robust to regression to the mean, multiple testing and placebo or shuffled-mix controls?
evidence_establishes: Nothing: retrieval returned no records, so no historical evidence was available for this question.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether this or a similar question was previously tested, and with what result.
Whether prior attempts hit problems such as low power, outcome-derived labels, leakage or team-quality confounding.
Whether any adherence metric or recommendation-construction method has been validated.
own_inferences: Adherence to a mix whose best/avoid labels are built from points per possession is partly mechanical: possessions of recommended types that score well also add to the margin, so adherence will correlate with winning even if the recommendation has no causal or predictive value (OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL).
Better teams may adhere more simply because they execute well or lead more, and score state affects play-type selection (reverse causation and CONFOUNDING).
54 series gives low power for a series-level effect; the many games in those series give more power, but games within a series are clustered and share the same opponent.
Suppression is conditional on the opponent defense, so the per-opponent possession counts behind each recommendation are likely small and noisy (MEASURE_RELIABILITY, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY).
A meaningful test requires recommendations built only from data prior to the game or series being predicted, plus a benchmark of adherence to naive mixes (league-average, own-season-average).
uncertainties: How adherence is defined (distance metric, mix granularity, which play types count).
How the suppression-conditional recommendation is built and which data window it uses.
Whether the 54 series are all playoff series across the seasons, and how many are partial for 2025-26.
The effect size that would matter practically.
No [prior work] were available, so there is no evidence on how noisy these estimates are in practice.

historical_effect.explanation: Retrieval returned an empty list, so the decision rests on first-principles assessment of the design and data. Absence of records does not show the question is novel or untried.

blocking_constraints.text: If best/avoid labels are derived from points scored in the same games or series being used to test winning, adherence is mechanically tied to the outcome. Labels must be built strictly out of sample.
54 series gives low power to detect a modest effect after adjusting for team quality; the game-level analysis must be clustered by series and gains less power than the game count suggests.
Team strength and game state drive both adherence and winning, so a raw association cannot be read as predictive value of the recommendation.

prior_work.summary: No earlier work was retrieved, so it is unknown whether this question has been studied. Nothing is claimed about earlier results.

risks.text: Recommendations based on points per possession are partly circular with winning; the test must use recommendations frozen before the evaluation games.
Building the mix from the same season or series as the evaluation games leaks future information. Use only prior games with a strict temporal cutoff, and avoid using the same series.
Team quality, opponent quality, home court, score state and injuries affect both mix and wins. Adjust with pre-series ratings, and treat game-state-driven shifts in play type as a bias.
Only 54 series; game-level analysis is clustered; the effect is likely small relative to noise.
Few prior possessions per team-opponent-play-type cell yield unstable suppression estimates and recommendations.
Split-half reliability of suppression-conditional recommendations is unknown and could be near zero; it must be established first.
Extreme best/avoid play types selected on noisy estimates will regress toward the mean, so out-of-sample benefit shrinks.
Without shuffled-recommendation or league-average-mix baselines, any adherence-wins association may reflect generic efficiency.
Many adherence definitions, thresholds, seasons and play types invite forking paths; fix one primary specification in advance.
Play-type distributions and defensive schemes change across 2022-26, so recommendations may not transfer across seasons.

design.estimand: Incremental predictive value of pre-registered adherence to an out-of-sample, opponent-conditional recommended play-type mix for game win probability (and series outcome as a secondary measure), beyond pre-game team and opponent strength, home court and a naive mix baseline.
design.unit: Primary: team-game, clustered by series and team. Secondary: series (n=54), which is underpowered and used descriptively.
design.sample: Playoff series in 2022-23 through 2025-26 (the 54 series as recorded). Regular-season games may be added for a larger, pre-registered robustness set. 2025-26 playoffs are used only once complete (from 2026-06-21), as a locked holdout; they are not used in tuning. Recommendations for each game use only prior games (rolling window, temporal cutoff before the series or game, no same-series data in the primary spec).
design.power: Run a simulation-based power analysis before looking at outcomes, using the observed game counts and a plausible effect (e.g. adherence moving win probability by 2-4 points per SD after adjustment). Report minimum detectable effect at the game level (cluster-adjusted) and the series level. First confirm split-half reliability of recommendations (e.g. correlation across odd/even games or across seasons). If reliability is below a threshold fixed in advance (e.g. 0.3) or the series-level minimum detectable effect is implausibly large, report as underpowered and do not make a confirmatory claim.
design.controls: Pre-series team ratings (net rating, opponent-adjusted), opponent rating, home court, rest, and availability of key players where it can be derived. Use first-half or non-garbage-time possessions to limit score-state reverse causation. Include a baseline of adherence to the league-average mix and to the team's own season-average mix. Fit a logistic model with cluster-robust errors (or mixed model) with a pre-specified adherence measure.
design.falsification: Placebo recommendations: shuffle best/avoid labels across opponents or play types and recompute adherence; use the recommendation for a different opponent; use future-shifted labels as a leakage check, which should show no extra [source] in the proper design. If the placebo adherence predicts wins as well as true adherence, the effect is attributed to generic efficiency or label circularity. Also test whether labels derived in-sample inflate the effect relative to out-of-sample labels, which quantifies the circularity.
design.multiplicity: One primary specification (single adherence metric, window, and model) fixed in a pre-registration before outcomes are examined. Secondary and exploratory analyses are labeled; apply Holm correction across secondary families.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if the out-of-sample adherence coefficient on game win is positive with a cluster-robust 95% CI excluding zero after controls, it exceeds the naive mix and placebo-shuffled distributions (p<0.05 vs placebo), it holds on the locked 2025-26 playoff holdout in direction, and reliability passes the preset threshold. Rejected only if the CI excludes effects at or above the pre-specified minimum interesting effect. Otherwise report inconclusive or underpowered. No claim from in-sample labels.
design.data_version: Per-game NBA stats API files and the play-type possession graph for 2022-23 through 2025-26 as available on 2026-06-16; freeze a dated snapshot and code hash before analysis. 2025-26 regular season complete from 2026-04-13; 2025-26 playoffs complete from 2026-06-21, so final analysis waits for that and is not run on partial data.
